items.l1-u01-p1: It is seven. I am in the kitchen with Dad. He has an egg and a red cup. The cup is on the table. We are ready for breakfast. I do not want tea. I want milk. Is it hot or cold? Dad says it is cold. I eat the egg at home.
items.l1-u01-p2: I am at the park with my sister. She is on a red bike, and I am in a little car. It is a toy car, but it is big for me. We do not go fast. Are we near the tree or the bus? We are near the tree.
items.l1-u02-p1: Today we have a class party. We put five red cups and four blue cups on the table. That is nine cups. What do we need now? We need cake, too. They bring the cake, and she brings water. Who has the plates? You do. Yes, we are ready.
items.l1-u02-p2: A girl and a boy are at the school store. She wants eight pencils, and he wants five pens. They see four red bags and nine blue bags. What bag do you like? The girl says, "That red bag." The boy says, "I like that bag, too."
items.l1-u03-p1: Today is sports day. Six kids run, and three kids sit by the tree. One boy has a red ball. Two girls have a blue ball. Now the teacher says, "Go!" Seven kids run to the line. Ten hands go up. Every kid wants to play.
items.l1-u03-p2: A baby, a boy, and a girl are at home. The girl has one paper hat. The boy has two toy cars. Now they play king and queen. The baby is the king. He sits on a big chair. Today, the three kids have fun together.
items.l1-u04-p1: Tom is at the school health room. His arm and leg hurt. His neck is fine, but one eye is red. The nurse looks at his ear, too. Tom is hot and sad. He sees a fat cat by the door. The cat makes him smile.
items.l1-u04-p2: A man is at the school door. His name is Mr. Brown. Mrs. Green is with him. They need help, so Ms. Hill comes. She says, "My name is Anna. Come with me." The man and Mrs. Green go to the school office. Now they are fine.
items.l1-u05-p1: Our dog is a good pet, but he likes to run. At the park, he sees a bird and runs to a tree. A cat is under the tree. The cat sees a pig on a card. Our dog sees it, too. He wants to play with them all.
items.l1-u05-p2: The sun is in the sky, and a bird sits in our tree. My cat looks up with her nose in the air. At night, the moon comes out. My little pet is sad because the bird is not there. I give her a lion toy, and she is happy.
items.l1-u06-p1: It is lunch time at home. Dad puts an egg and rice on my plate. Mom gives me a cup of water. My sister has milk, and Grandma has tea. A pie is on the table, too. We have good food. We sit down and eat lunch together.
items.l1-u06-p2: My room is ready for art time. A pen and a cup are on my desk. I draw a picture of a red ball by my bed. Then I draw milk, tea, and an egg. The picture is for Mom. I put it on her door.
items.l1-u07-p1: I come home at four. My dog and I go to the park. I jog, and he can run. We love this game. Then I sit by the door and watch him. I miss Mom, but she comes home soon. We all go into the room together.
items.l1-u07-p2: A toy car is in my room. I sit on the bed and make it go. The car runs to the door. Now it is under a toy bus. Dad comes home and looks in. "Come with me," he says. We go to the real car and ride to Grandma's home.
items.l1-u08-p1: I see a new bike at the store. It is big, red, and very nice. Dad says the bike is good, but it is too tall for me. A small bike is here. It is not new, but it is great. I can ride it well, so we take it home.
items.l1-u08-p2: Today I walk to school with Mom. The new guard has a big job. He stands here by the red door and helps us. A boy has a bad fall, but he is okay. The guard is nice to him. "No running," he says. We walk into school.
items.l2-u01-p1: It is my birthday, and our classroom is very busy. The clock is on the wall, and the party is at three. These red cups are on the table. Those blue plates are under the table. Please put them next to the real cake. My classmate writes "Happy Birthday" in English. Dad says its color is very nice.
items.l2-u01-p2: Our class has a special day about places. These students have flags, and those students have maps. One map is of the USA. Another card says ROC. Please put each card on the right desk, not under it. Our teacher checks the clock. We have one hour, and the room is very busy.
items.l2-u02-p1: Our school has a family music show. My sister is a singer, and my brother plays the drum. My father sits with my little son. A woman helps each student get ready. My classmate stands by our teacher. The air in the hall is cool. After the song, every family smiles and claps.
items.l2-u02-p2: A teacher takes her class outside for nature week. One student sees an ant on a flower. Another child finds a bee in the air. My classmate shows me his toe because an ant is near it. A woman helps him stand up. We laugh and talk about the small animals we see this year.
items.l2-u03-p1: Our class visits a small zoo. A cow and a sheep eat near the tree. A hen walks by the flower, and a frog sits under it. We see a fox, a hippo, and many birds. At lunch, we eat fruit by the sea animal room. Then we draw our favorite animal in a book.
items.l2-u03-p2: Today our classroom becomes an animal art room. Each student takes a book from the box and sits on a chair. I draw a fox near a flower. My friend draws a frog by the sea. The teacher adds a cow, a hen, a hippo, and a sheep to one big zoo picture. We put it on the classroom wall.
items.l2-u04-p1: We stop at a convenience store after school. I want an apple and a ham sandwich. My sister wants candy, cake, and cola. Dad says we need real food, so we get rice and a salad, too. Mom does not drink coffee or Coke at night. She takes water. We eat together at the table.
items.l2-u04-p2: Our class makes a food book. I use a pencil and ruler to draw a long table. Amy uses glue for the apple and cake pictures. We read each page and write one food word. At lunch, we eat rice and ham at school. After lunch, we study the new words and put the book by the classroom door.
items.l2-u05-p1: At lunch, Mom gives me a bowl of rice and soup. I close my book and sit on the sofa. My sister makes a sandwich and puts on her cap. We see a ship from the window. I sing a song about the sea, and she plays with her doll. Then we wash our bowls and go to the store.
items.l2-u05-p2: A small store has a school play today. One child wears a short shirt and a red cap. Another child sits on a sofa with a doll. I give them a toy ship for the show. They sing, play, and see their teacher smile. After the show, we close the door and share soup and sandwiches.
items.l2-u06-p1: Our classroom is dirty after art class, and everyone is busy. I wash the gray table while my friendly classmate picks up paper. The old box is brown, and the new box is green. We talk about where things go. A shy girl wants to help, so she stands by me. Soon the room looks very clean.
items.l2-u06-p2: Mia wants a cute shirt for the school show. She tries a pink one, but it is very short. The black shirt is old and dirty. A friendly worker shows her a green shirt with brown buttons. Mia is shy, so Mom talks for her. She stands by the mirror and wants the green one. They wash it at home.
items.l2-u07-p1: We have a picnic by the school. I say hello to a shy girl in a white cap. She says hi, but she talks very slowly. We show her our small yellow ball and green cups. "Wow, I like the colors," she says. We thank her and ask her to sing a song. Soon we are all friends.
items.l2-u07-p2: A small boy comes to the music room. "Hey, what is your favorite color?" I ask. He says yellow, but his guitar is white. "Oh, it is very nice!" I say. He is shy and plays a slow song. At the end, everyone says, "Wow!" The boy smiles and says, "Thank you."
items.l3-u01-p1: At eleven a.m., our English teacher gives us a new word. We read it together and ask what it is about. Ben knows where it is in the book, but he does not know why it is there. After an hour, we can say the word and write it. Every child feels great because what we say is true. We will study together every afternoon.
items.l3-u01-p2: Two hours ago, Amy called me after school. She wanted help with three English words, so she walked to my home. We read the words with my sister in the afternoon. When the sun was down, Amy asked where she could put her book. I put her book in a bag. In the evening, she walked home and said, "I know every word now." I said, "Great!" because it was true.
items.l3-u02-p1: Yesterday morning, my aunt and uncle came to our house at eight o'clock. Dad made breakfast, and every child helped. My brother gave the children milk, and I put food on the table. My uncle is a worker, so he had to go at eleven a.m. Before he went, Daddy took a family picture. We said good-bye and asked him to come again in one week.
items.l3-u02-p2: Our school family day started at two p.m. yesterday. My friend Ben came with his dad, aunt, and two children. His daddy helped the teacher, and my family made drinks. At three o'clock, the children started to run. Ben was slow, but his friend helped him. They tried to run together. Every child said their run was great, even with zero prizes.
items.l3-u03-p1: The weather was hot when our teacher took us to the zoo. I saw a big elephant take food with its nose. A child asked why the animal had no hair on its body. A duck put its head down and sat under a tree. I put my hand in my bag and found an apple. I was hungry, so I ate it with my lunch.
items.l3-u03-p2: Ben and I went to the sea with a kite. The weather was fine, so Ben started to run. The kite went up, but it came down into a tree. Ben was sad and put his head on my arm. I asked him to help me. He took my hand, and we got it down together. The kite was fine. A star was in the evening sky when we walked home.
items.l3-u04-p1: Before school, Mia ate a banana and drank milk for breakfast. In the classroom, the teacher asked the children to write about their food. Mia had a computer, but she could not spell banana. She asked a friend and then wrote the word. Her eraser fell under the desk. She found it with an old cookie under the desk. The teacher said, "Please do not eat cookies in the classroom."
items.l3-u04-p2: Dad and I made beef and rice for dinner. My sister made cold drinks with juice and ice. She gave me a cookie, but I wanted it after dinner. While Dad made the food, I used the computer to learn a new English word. I wrote it on a card and asked my sister to spell it. She spelled it well, so I gave her two cookies after we ate.
items.l3-u05-p1: It was hot after school, so Amy came to my house. We went into the kitchen and made ice cream with milk and ice. I put in too much salt, but Amy said it was still good. We took the ice cream and juice to the dining room. Dad came home with hot dogs for dinner. We ate together and gave him a big cup of ice cream.
items.l3-u05-p2: Mia wanted to wear her new dress to a family dinner. The weather was cold, so her aunt gave her a coat and a red hat. Before they left the house, the telephone rang in the dining room. Her uncle was on the phone. He asked Mia to call him on her phone when they got there. Mia said yes, put on her coat, and walked out with her aunt.
items.l3-u06-p1: My friend Sam came from America for a family trip. Dad did not drive because we wanted to take a train to the sea. On the train, Sam saw a bird fly in the sky. When we got there, we saw a big truck at a store. Dad called his friend, and the man gave us two bicycles. We had a great afternoon on the bikes.
items.l3-u06-p2: Emma wanted to try her new bicycle after school. Dad helped her get on the bike, and she started to go. A truck came by, so Dad asked her to wait. When it was gone, Emma tried again. She went too fast, and her bike went into a tree. She did not cry because her arm and leg were fine. Dad called home and said, "Emma can go now!"
items.l3-u07-p1: In autumn, our school asked families to join a dance. I invited my friend Lily because she wanted to try it. We needed two hats, so we made them with old cards. Lily helped me, and we waited for the glue to dry. At school, the teacher asked us to dance together. We tried three times. After the dance, I took the hats home.
items.l3-u07-p2: Dad came home from work and said he needed help. Our dog was dirty after a walk, so we had to wash and dry it. I took water, and Dad made a warm bed. The dog tried to run, but Dad asked it to wait. When its hair was dry, I kissed its head. The dog went to sleep, and Dad said we did great work.
items.l3-u08-p1: At school, we made a store with toys and books. I had ten dollars in play money. I looked down and saw a car under the table. "Oops, is there any money with it?" I asked. Ben said, "Uh-uh, but the car is one dollar." I really wanted it, so I gave him one dollar. Then we put everything up and said good-bye.
items.l3-u08-p2: Emma and I were singing together in her room. Her baby brother was sleeping, so we had to sing slowly. Then Emma stood up, but I looked down at the words. "Oh-oh, I do not know this word," I said. Emma said it with me, and I could sing again. Her brother opened his eyes. "Oops!" we said, and we gave him a toy.
items.l4-u01-p1: Our class made a paper for sports day. I wrote the date on it, but I wrote it wrong. The paper said the game was on the eighteenth. Amy said the date was the fifteenth. She does not like to speak to a big class, so I told the teacher for her. We made a new paper and put it on the wall. Some students came to read it. Now everyone knows which day is right.
items.l4-u01-p2: My father asked me to speak to my uncle on the phone. My uncle lives far from us. He said he will come on the eighteenth and stay for some days. I asked which train he takes. He said the one at eight. I wrote this on paper so I will not get the date wrong. My mother was happy. She says my uncle is very funny.
items.l4-u02-p1: My grandmother is seventy this year. My mother is forty and my father is fifty. I am thirteen. We made a big card with all the numbers on it. My little sister put fourteen flowers on the front. I asked my grandmother if she was happy. She said she never counts her years. She only counts her friends. That was a good answer, and I still think about it now.
items.l4-u02-p2: Our teacher asked us to count to ninety. Ben stopped at sixteen because he could not think. I helped him from seventeen to thirty. Then he went on to sixty by himself. After that he did nineteen and forty with no help. The teacher said he did well and gave him a book. Ben was very happy. He said he will never stop at sixteen again.
items.l4-u03-p1: My grandpa is a writer. He writes at home every morning. My grandma helps him read his work. On the weekend my parents take me to see them. My grandma made a cake for me because I am twelve now. My grandpa gave me a book about a butterfly. I read it that night in my room. After that I was very thirsty and drank some water.
items.l4-u03-p2: We went to the zoo with my grandmother on the weekend. We saw a big panda eat its lunch. A man said good morning to my grandfather and called him sir. My grandfather was happy all day. Twenty children came with their parents too. It was hot and we were thirsty, so we sat under a tree. Tomorrow I will draw the panda for my grandma.
items.l4-u04-p1: We had art class after reading class today. I took out my pencil box and found my crayon was gone. Ben let me use his paint. I made a drawing of a snake on my paper. The wind came in the window and moved my page. My drawing fell down, but it was not wet. The teacher put it on the wall for everyone to see.
items.l4-u04-p2: My homework was to write every letter of the alphabet. I did the first page at school and the second page at home. My pencil case was in my bag, so I used a pen. After that we went to the bookstore. My mother bought me a new pencil box and some bread. I ate the bread on the bus and read my new book.
items.l4-u05-p1: My mother made dinner for us today. She put a big dish of salad on the table. My father made pork and a small steak. I do not like vegetable soup, so I said it was yucky. My mother said the salad was yummy and I should try it. I did try it, and it was good. After dinner we had a sweet snack with a little sugar.
items.l4-u05-p2: We went to the bank with my father on Saturday. A man there gave me a red balloon. After that we went home and I called my friend on my cellphone. I asked her to come to my house for a snack. We ate bread and one small dish of fruit. It was sweet and yummy. Then we went out to feed the birds near my window.
items.l4-u06-p1: My father works in an office in the city. On Saturday we took the bus to see him. We got off at the bus stop near his office. The light in his room was on and the window was open. He put some tape on a box for me and gave me a pen. After that we went to a restaurant on the road near the station.
items.l4-u06-p2: Our television is on the wall in the living room. My little brother watches TV after school every day. Today the TV was off because my mother wanted a quiet house. My brother put his socks on and we went out. We walked down the road to the station and back. He said the city is very big at night. My sister wore her new skirt.
items.l4-u07-p1: We went to the beach and I did not want to swim at first. The water was cold, so I stayed on the sand. My sister said the water was better after some minutes. I did use her hat because the sun was hot. Then we did dig a big hole in the sand. My father said we should stop before lunch. It was the best day.
items.l4-u07-p2: My mother sent me to buy some bread on the street near our house. She gave me money to pay for it. I did not worry because I go there often. On the way I saw my friend and we did stop to talk. I told her we will visit my aunt tomorrow. She said her cat did fall from a chair but was fine.
items.l4-u08-p1: The weather was warm and sunny on Sunday. We went to the park and it was very cool under the trees. My friend Amy has long hair and she wore a pretty blue dress. She is smart and very funny too. We saw a strong man carry two big boxes to a car. I was sure he was tired after that. It was a wonderful day.
items.l4-u08-p2: My little brother and I have the same shoes. His are small and mine are long. He fell in the water and his socks were wet. He was not sad because the day was warm. He is young, but he is strong. My mother said he is a funny child. We told her it was a wonderful day, and she said she was sure of that.
items.l4-u09-p1: Summer vacation is my favorite season. In summer we swim every day and eat ice after lunch. In winter there is snow on the hills near my home. In spring we see flowers on the way to school. My father reads the newspaper for the news about the weather. He said tomorrow will be a good day for sport, so we will play soccer in the park.
items.l4-u09-p2: We went to see a movie on Saturday with my cousin. Before the movie we played soccer in the park. My cousin is very good at that sport. After the movie we went home and my mother put on a CD. My sister likes dancing to it. The news said there will be snow this winter. We want to see the snow in our vacation.
items.l4-u10-p1: We had a party for Chinese New Year at my grandma's house. My little kitten sat next to me all night. My mother put red paper in front of the door. Even my father made a dish for us. The food had a very good smell. We ate a big part of it and left a little on the table. Out on the road I could hear children play.
items.l4-u10-p2: Our school has a sports day every spring. This year I did not know my shoe size, so my mother took me out to buy new ones. On the day I ran in two sports and did swimming after. My kitty came to the door when I got home. She made a small sound and sat next to my bag. Even my sister said I did well.
